recipes.name: Bánh Mì Thịt
recipes.flavorProfile: A crackling, airy baguette layered with rich pâté, cool pork roll, roast pork belly, tangy pickles, cucumber, cilantro and a bite of chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings protein from three kinds of pork and some iron and vitamin A from the liver pâté, with the pickles and fresh herbs adding crunch; it is a rich, salty sandwich best eaten as a full meal.

components.note: split along one side, warmed until crisp
about 30 g spread inside each roll
about 50 g sliced thin for each sandwich
about 1 tbsp per roll
about 0.25 cup per sandwich, drained

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Rub the pork belly flesh with fish sauce, sugar, garlic and pepper, rub the scored skin with salt, and leave it uncovered in the fridge 2 to 12 hours.
Roast the pork skin side up at 400°F (200°C) for 40 to 50 minutes, until the skin blisters and the meat is cooked through. Rest it 10 minutes and slice thin.
Warm the baguettes at 350°F (180°C) for 3 to 5 minutes until the crust crackles, then split each one along one side.
Spread pâté on one inner face and mayonnaise on the other.
Layer in chả lụa, roast pork, cucumber, pickled carrot and daikon, cilantro and chili.
Shake a few drops of Maggi over the filling, close the roll and eat it while the bread is still crisp.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the roast pork belly, chả lụa and pâté.
From the liver in the pâté.
A little from the cucumber, pickles, herbs and chili.

citations.source: Helen's Recipes, Bánh Mì Thịt Nguội

recipes.curationNote: Helen's thịt nguội layering (pâté, chả lụa, pork belly, pickles, cucumber, cilantro, chili) followed, with the roast belly as the cooked meat; Vicky Pham's overview confirms the mayo and Maggi finish.

recipes.name: Bánh Mì Xíu Mại
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft pork and shrimp meatballs in a sweet, garlicky tomato sauce, spooned into a crisp roll so the bread soaks up the sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: The pork and shrimp bring protein and the tomato sauce adds lycopene and some vitamin C; the baguette makes it a filling, carb-heavy breakfast.

components.note: split and warmed
a small handful per sandwich

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Mix the pork, shrimp, half the onion, jicama, salt, pepper, fish sauce, sugar, potato starch and scallion until tacky, and roll into balls about 3 cm across.
Steam the meatballs 10 to 12 minutes until firm, so they hold their shape in the sauce.
Heat the oil, fry the garlic and remaining onion 2 to 3 minutes, add the tomatoes and cook until they slump, 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the water, sugar, salt and fish sauce, slide in the meatballs and simmer 15 to 20 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Split the warm rolls, spoon in 3 or 4 meatballs with sauce, and top with pickles, cucumber and cilantro.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork and shrimp meatballs.
From the tomatoes cooked down in the sauce.

recipes.curationNote: Single recipe source (Vicky Pham) for the meatballs and sauce, served in the Đà Lạt and central breakfast way inside bánh mì. Region set Central since the sandwich is most associated with Đà Lạt in the Central Highlands.

recipes.name: Bánh Mì Ốp La
recipes.flavorProfile: Runny fried eggs with lacy edges, seasoned with Maggi and black pepper, tucked into a crisp roll with cucumber, cilantro and chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: The eggs bring protein, choline and vitamin B12 for a quick breakfast; the roll supplies most of the energy.

components.note: split and warmed

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Heat the oil in a small pan over medium high until it shimmers.
Crack in 2 eggs and fry 2 to 3 minutes, until the edges crisp and the yolks stay soft. Repeat with the other 2.
Shake Maggi over the eggs and grind on black pepper.
Slide 2 eggs into each warm roll and add cucumber, cilantro and chili.
recipes.curationNote: Written mostly from description: no dedicated recipe page was opened. Wikipedia notes bánh mì eaten with fried eggs at breakfast; Vicky Pham covers the bread and Maggi. Eggs, Maggi, pepper, cucumber, cilantro and chili is the standard street version.

recipes.name: Gỏi Cuốn (Fresh Spring Rolls)
recipes.flavorProfile: Cool, chewy rice paper wrapped around poached pork, pink shrimp, soft noodles, lettuce and mint, dipped into a thick sweet peanut hoisin sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean protein from shrimp and pork with fresh lettuce and herbs, and nothing fried; the dip carries most of the sugar and salt.

components.note: about 1 tbsp per roll, for dipping

ingredients.prepNote: peeled and halved lengthwise after cooking

instructions: Simmer the pork belly with the onion and salt in water to cover for 25 to 30 minutes until a skewer goes in cleanly; cool and slice paper thin.
Drop the shrimp into the same simmering water for 2 to 3 minutes, until pink, then peel and halve each one lengthwise.
Boil the vermicelli 3 to 5 minutes, rinse in cold water and drain well.
Dip one sheet of rice paper in warm water for 2 to 3 seconds and lay it flat; it softens as you fill it.
Lay 3 shrimp halves cut side up in a row, then lettuce, noodles, mint and pork. Fold the sides in, roll tightly, and tuck a chive in so it pokes out of one end.
Serve right away with the peanut hoisin dip.

citations.source: Hungry Huy, How to Make Gỏi Cuốn

recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy amounts kept for 10 rolls: half a pound each of pork belly and shrimp, a third of a pack of bún. The dip is the shared peanut hoisin base.

recipes.name: Chả Giò (Fried Spring Rolls)
recipes.flavorProfile: Shatteringly crisp golden rolls packed with juicy pork, glass noodles and crunchy wood ear, wrapped in lettuce and herbs and dunked in nước chấm.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings protein from the pork, but deep frying makes these a rich treat; wrapping them in lettuce and herbs adds fresh greens to each bite.

components.note: about 1 tbsp per roll, for dipping

ingredients.baseName: Mushrooms, tree ears, Cloud ear, dried
Glass noodles made from mung bean starch
ingredients.cutPrep: soaked and cut in short lengths

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

ingredients.name: spring roll wrappers
ingredients.prepNote: wheat wrappers; rice paper is the other traditional choice
for deep frying; much of it stays in the pan

instructions: Mix the pork, wood ear, glass noodles, scallion, onion, sugar, pepper, sesame oil, salt and oyster sauce until evenly combined.
Lay a wrapper with a corner toward you, put a heaped tablespoon of filling near that corner and shape it into a log.
Fold the bottom corner over, fold in the sides, roll tightly and seal the last corner with egg yolk. Repeat with the rest.
Heat the oil to 325°F (165°C) and fry the rolls in batches for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack, then wrap each roll in lettuce with mint and perilla and dip it in nước chấm.

nutritionHighlights.note: Mostly from the pork and the frying oil.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Vietnamese Egg Rolls (Chả Giò)

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham's 30-roll batch kept as written (2 lb pork, wood ear, glass noodles, oyster sauce, yolk seal). Oil for deep frying listed at 750 ml; actual absorption is far less.

recipes.name: Bánh Xèo (Crispy Pancakes)
recipes.flavorProfile: A sizzling, lacy yellow crêpe of rice flour, turmeric and coconut, folded over pork, shrimp and bean sprouts, then torn and rolled in mustard greens and herbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: Protein from pork and shrimp with a big pile of sprouts, greens and herbs; the coconut cream and frying oil make it a rich dish.

components.note: about 2 tbsp per pancake

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, wheat flour, turmeric, water, coconut cream and salt into a thin batter, stir in the scallion and rest it 30 minutes.
Steam the soaked mung beans 15 to 20 minutes until soft.
Heat a 25 cm pan over high with a little oil, add a few slices of pork, 2 or 3 shrimp and some onion, and cook 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour in a ladle of batter and swirl it so it climbs the sides; it should sizzle loudly. Scatter a spoon of mung beans and a handful of sprouts over half.
Cover 2 to 3 minutes, then uncover and cook another 3 to 5 minutes until the edges are crisp and lift away. Fold in half and slide out.
Repeat with the rest. Eat torn into pieces, wrapped in mustard greens with herbs, and dipped in nước chấm.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork belly, shrimp and mung beans.
From the mustard greens and herbs.
From the coconut cream and pork belly.

recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy amounts for 12 crêpes kept; fluid ounces converted to ml (28 fl oz water, 14 fl oz coconut cream). Southern style with coconut and mustard greens.

recipes.name: Bánh Khọt
recipes.flavorProfile: Bite-size cups of rice and coconut batter, crisp outside and custardy inside, each crowned with a shrimp and scallion oil, wrapped in lettuce and dipped.
recipes.healthBenefit: A shrimp on each cake brings a little protein and the lettuce and herbs add freshness; the coconut milk and pan oil make these a rich snack.

components.note: spooned over the cakes
about 1 tbsp per cake

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

ingredients.prepNote: for the cups of the pan

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, cornstarch, water, coconut milk, turmeric, salt and scallion into a smooth batter and rest it 30 minutes.
Heat a bánh khọt or aebleskiver pan over medium high and put about half a teaspoon of oil in each cup.
Fill each cup nearly to the top with batter; it should sizzle. Cover and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Press a shrimp into each cake, cover again and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until the bottoms are golden and crisp.
Lift out, spoon scallion oil over, and serve wrapped in lettuce and herbs with nước chấm.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the shrimp on each cake.
From the coconut milk in the batter.

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham's 14-piece batter followed (1 cup rice flour, coconut milk, turmeric, one shrimp per cake). Vũng Tàu is the home of the dish, in the south.

recipes.name: Bánh Cuốn
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, almost translucent steamed rice sheets rolled around savory pork and wood ear, topped with fried shallots and served with chả lụa and nước chấm.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, steamed dish with protein from the pork and chả lụa; the fried shallots and dipping sauce add the salt.

components.note: about 50 g sliced per plate
about 1 tbsp scattered over each plate
about 3 tbsp per plate

ingredients.baseName: Mushrooms, tree ears, Cloud ear, dried

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, salt, oil and water into a thin batter and rest it 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Heat the oil, cook the garlic and onion 2 minutes, add the pork and wood ear with salt, sugar and pepper and cook 5 to 7 minutes until dry and crumbly.
Brush a nonstick pan lightly with oil over medium heat, pour in a thin layer of batter, swirl, cover and steam 30 to 60 seconds until the sheet turns clear.
Turn the sheet onto an oiled tray, spoon a line of filling along one edge and roll it up. Repeat with the rest.
Plate the rolls with lettuce, sprouts, cucumber and sliced chả lụa, scatter fried shallots over, and pour nước chấm alongside.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork filling and chả lụa.
From the rice and tapioca sheets.

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham's nonstick pan method and 5-serving amounts followed. Northern dish (Thanh Trì, Hà Nội), served as a plated breakfast, so side/main.

recipes.name: Phở Cuốn
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, wide sheets of fresh phở noodle rolled around garlicky stir-fried beef, lettuce and herbs, dipped in sweet sour nước chấm.
recipes.healthBenefit: The beef brings protein, iron and zinc, and the fresh herbs and lettuce add greens; nothing is fried in deep oil.

components.note: about 2 tbsp per serving, for dipping

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, water, salt and oil and rest the batter 30 minutes.
Marinate the beef with garlic, ginger, fish sauce and pepper for 15 minutes.
Steam thin sheets of batter in a covered oiled pan for 1 to 2 minutes each, until clear, and stack them on an oiled tray. Cut each sheet into a rectangle about 15 by 20 cm.
Heat the oil over high, stir-fry the onion 1 minute, add the beef and cook 1 to 2 minutes, just until it loses its pink.
Lay lettuce, herbs and a spoon of beef on each sheet and roll it up tightly.
Serve with nước chấm for dipping.

citations.source: Helen's Recipes, Fresh Rice Noodle Rolls (Phở Cuốn)

recipes.curationNote: Single source (Helen's Recipes), a Hà Nội dish from Ngũ Xã. Rump beef is matched to beef round.

recipes.name: Bò Bía
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft rice paper rolls of sweet braised jicama and carrot, Chinese sausage, egg ribbons and dried shrimp, dipped in hoisin with crushed peanuts.
recipes.healthBenefit: The jicama and carrot bring fibre and vitamin A, and the eggs and dried shrimp add protein; the sausage and hoisin make it salty and sweet.

ingredients.prepNote: cooked as a thin omelette and sliced

instructions: Heat the oil, fry the dried shrimp 1 minute, add the jicama, carrot and salt and stir-fry 5 to 8 minutes until tender but not mushy. Cool.
Pan-fry the sausage slices 2 to 3 minutes, and cook the eggs as a thin omelette and slice it into ribbons.
Warm the garlic in a little oil, then stir in the hoisin, water and sugar and simmer 1 minute for the sauce.
Dip a sheet of rice paper, lay on lettuce, a spoon of jicama, sausage and egg, and roll tightly.
Serve with the hoisin sauce topped with crushed peanuts.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggs, sausage and dried shrimp.

recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy for 4 servings; three rolls each. The Hokkien popiah came to Sài Gòn with Chinese Vietnamese cooks.

recipes.name: Bánh Bột Lọc
recipes.flavorProfile: Clear, chewy tapioca dumplings showing an orange shrimp and pork filling, steamed in banana leaf and eaten with sweet fish sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: A small amount of protein from shrimp and pork in a mostly starchy dumpling; good as a snack rather than a meal.

components.note: about 1.5 tsp per dumpling

ingredients.name: banana leaves
ingredients.cutPrep: cut in 15 cm squares, wiped and softened over heat

instructions: Warm the oil with the annatto seeds 1 to 2 minutes until deep orange, then strain out the seeds.
Fry the shallot and garlic in the annatto oil, add the pork belly and dried shrimp and cook 5 to 7 minutes, seasoning with fish sauce, sugar and pepper.
Pour the boiling water over the tapioca starch and salt, stir, then add the cool water and knead into a smooth, soft dough.
Flatten small balls of dough into rounds, put a piece of pork and a shrimp on each, fold into a half moon and pinch shut.
Wrap each dumpling in a banana leaf square and steam 15 to 20 minutes, until the dough turns clear.
Serve warm with sweetened fish sauce.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the dried shrimp and pork.

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham amounts for 30 Huế dumplings (14 oz tapioca, 1.5 cups boiling water). Dipping sauce is the nước chấm base.

recipes.name: Bánh Bèo
recipes.flavorProfile: Tiny, soft rice cakes steamed in saucers, topped with pink shrimp floss, crisp pork rind bits and scallion oil, eaten with a spoonful of fish sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, steamed rice snack; the shrimp topping brings protein and the fish sauce most of the salt.

components.note: spooned over the cakes
about 2 tbsp per plate

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, water, salt and oil and let the batter rest at least 1 hour.
Oil small saucers, heat them in the steamer 2 minutes, then fill each with a thin layer of batter and steam 5 to 7 minutes until set and slightly hollow in the middle.
Cook the shrimp in a dry pan with fish sauce and sugar 4 to 5 minutes, then pound or pulse into fluffy floss.
Top each cake with shrimp floss, crushed pork rind and scallion oil.
Spoon a little fish sauce over each cake and eat it straight from the saucer.
recipes.curationNote: Helen's Huế batter (400 g rice flour, 100 g tapioca, 1 L water) and shrimp topping; Vicky Pham's page (partly read) confirms scallion oil and fried pork rind. Six plates of 8 cakes.

recipes.name: Nem Nướng Cuốn
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, springy grilled pork sausage rolled in rice paper with crisp rice paper, green banana, star fruit, herbs and lettuce, dipped in a thick pâté and peanut sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Grilled pork brings protein and the raw fruit, herbs and greens bring fibre and vitamin C; the dipping sauce is rich, so a little goes far.

components.note: about 90 g worked into the dipping sauce

ingredients.cutPrep: boiled 5 minutes and cut in tiny dice

ingredients.name: green banana
ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and cut in thin strips

instructions: Mix the pork with fish sauce, tapioca starch, baking powder, sugar, half the shallot and half the garlic, then fold in the diced fat. Chill 1 hour.
With oiled hands, press the mixture onto skewers or shape into fingers, and grill over hot coals 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.

For the sauce, fry the rest of the shallot and garlic, add the pâté, peanut butter, fish sauce and the water whisked with the glutinous rice flour, and simmer 3 to 5 minutes until thick. Top with sesame and peanuts.
Roll each nem in a sheet of dampened rice paper with lettuce, herbs, cucumber, banana, star fruit, pineapple and mango.
Dip into the warm sauce.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the star fruit, pineapple, mango and herbs.
From the green banana, fruit and greens.

citations.source: Helen's Recipes, Grilled Pork Skewer (Nem Nướng)
Vicky Pham, Nem Nướng Nha Trang

recipes.curationNote: Helen's nem itself (600 g pork, fat, baking powder, tapioca) and her pâté and peanut sauce, compared against Vicky Pham's Nha Trang assembly and glutinous rice sauce. Region Central (Huế and Nha Trang). Crispy rice paper (ram) left out for simplicity.

recipes.name: Thịt Kho Trứng (Caramelized Pork and Eggs)
recipes.flavorProfile: Meltingly soft pork belly and eggs braised in coconut water and caramel until glossy, sweet and salty, spooned over plain rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Rich in protein from the pork and eggs, with B vitamins and choline from the eggs; the pork belly makes it a fatty, salty dish for the Tết table or a cold day.

components.note: about 4 tbsp of caramel
steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.prepNote: fresh coconut water (nước dừa); coconut soda is the common stand-in abroad

instructions: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 3 to 5 minutes, drain and rinse off the scum.
Put the pork in a heavy pot with the caramel, fish sauce, salt and onion and toss over medium heat 5 minutes until coated.
Add the coconut water and enough water to just cover, bring to a boil, skim, and simmer uncovered 1 to 1.5 hours.
Add the peeled eggs and simmer 30 to 45 minutes more, until the pork is tender and the eggs are amber.
Taste for salt, skim off some of the fat if you like, and serve with rice and pickled vegetables.
recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy amounts (2 lb pork, belly and shoulder, 8 eggs, 4 tbsp nước màu) followed. Coconut soda written as coconut water, the traditional liquid in the south.

recipes.name: Cá Kho Tộ (Clay Pot Caramelized Fish)
recipes.flavorProfile: Catfish steaks simmered down in a clay pot with dark caramel and fish sauce until sticky, peppery and deeply savory, eaten with rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Catfish brings protein, vitamin B12 and some omega-3 fats; the glaze is salty and sweet, so it is eaten in small amounts with lots of rice and vegetables.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tbsp in the marinade, 2 tbsp for the caramel
fresh coconut water (nước dừa); coconut soda is the common stand-in abroad

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Marinate the catfish with the fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, shallot and garlic for 30 minutes.
In a clay pot or heavy pan, cook the oil and remaining 2 tbsp sugar over medium heat 3 to 5 minutes, until the caramel is a deep amber.
Lay in the fish with its marinade, turn once to coat, and pour in the coconut water.
Simmer uncovered over low heat 30 to 40 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until it reduces to a thick glaze.
Finish with scallion, chili and plenty of black pepper, and serve in the pot with rice.
recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, 4 servings; 3 lb catfish written as 1300 g bone-in steaks. Catfish is not in the food database. A Mekong Delta clay-pot dish.

recipes.name: Gà Kho Gừng (Ginger Braised Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bone-in chicken braised with a lot of ginger in caramel and fish sauce until sticky, warm and peppery.
recipes.healthBenefit: The chicken brings protein and niacin, and the generous ginger adds warmth and aroma; the sauce is salty, so the rice and greens alongside matter.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.cutPrep: bone in, chopped in 5 cm pieces

ingredients.prepNote: 2 tbsp in the marinade, 2 tbsp for the caramel
fresh coconut water (nước dừa); coconut soda is the common stand-in abroad

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Marinate the chicken with 2 tbsp sugar, fish sauce, pepper, half the ginger, garlic and shallot for 30 minutes.
Cook the oil and remaining 2 tbsp sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat 3 to 5 minutes into a deep amber caramel.
Add the rest of the ginger, then the chicken, and turn it in the caramel 3 to 5 minutes.
Pour in the coconut water, cover and simmer 20 minutes, then uncover and cook 10 to 15 minutes more until the sauce is thick.
Top with cilantro, scallion and chili and serve with rice.
recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, 3 lb chicken, 3-inch ginger piece (about 40 g). Coconut water used for the liquid, as her recipe allows water or coconut soda.

recipes.name: Bò Lúc Lắc (Shaking Beef)
recipes.flavorProfile: Seared cubes of ribeye shaken in a hot wok with garlic and oyster sauce, tossed with onion and peppers, served with tomato rice and a lime pepper dip.
recipes.healthBenefit: A good share of protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12 from the beef, with vitamin C from the peppers and tomato; ribeye makes it a rich plate.

components.note: cooked rice, fried with tomato paste
for dipping the beef

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.prepNote: part of it infused with the garlic

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Toss the beef with oyster sauce, soy sauce, half the garlic, sugar and cornstarch and leave 30 minutes.
Fry the rest of the garlic in 2 tbsp oil until golden, strain it out and keep the garlic oil.
Fry the rice in a little garlic oil with the tomato paste 3 to 5 minutes until evenly red.
Heat a wok until smoking, add a little oil and the beef in one layer, sear 1 minute without moving, then shake the pan 1 to 2 minutes for medium rare. Lift out.
Stir-fry the onion, pepper and scallion 1 minute, return the beef and the garlic oil and toss.
Serve on lettuce and tomato with the tomato rice and the salt, pepper and lime dip.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the bell pepper and tomato.

recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy for 2 servings, with his tomato rice. The salt, pepper and lime dip is the muối tiêu chanh base.

recipes.name: Bò Kho (Beef Stew)
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender beef shank and carrots in a red, aromatic broth of lemongrass, star anise and tomato, eaten with crusty bread or noodles and Thai basil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef shank brings protein, collagen, iron and zinc, and the carrots add vitamin A; a warming, filling stew.

components.note: one roll per bowl, for dipping
about 2 cups of chicken broth

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.name: lemongrass
ingredients.cutPrep: stalks bruised and cut in 10 cm lengths

ingredients.prepNote: fresh coconut water (nước dừa); coconut soda is the common stand-in abroad

instructions: Toss the beef with salt, soy sauce, hoisin, half the garlic, paprika and curry powder and marinate at least 1 hour.
Brown the beef in the oil in batches, 5 to 7 minutes, then fry the onion, ginger, the rest of the garlic and the lemongrass 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, dark soy, star anise and bay leaves, return the beef, and add the broth, coconut water and water.
Simmer covered 1.5 to 2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Add the carrots and simmer 20 to 30 minutes more, until soft. Take out the lemongrass, anise and bay.
Serve with Thai basil and warm bánh mì, or over rice noodles.
recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy for 8 servings. The 2 cups of chicken broth point at the chicken phở broth base. Written as builderType soup since it is eaten in bowls, kept on the dishes.json shelf.

recipes.name: Gà Xào Sả Ớt (Lemongrass Chili Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bite-size chicken stir-fried with a heap of fragrant lemongrass, garlic and chili until golden and slightly sticky, salty sweet and hot.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean protein from the chicken with the aroma of lemongrass and chili; a quick weeknight dish to pair with rice and greens.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.cutPrep: boned and cut in bite-size pieces

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Marinate the chicken with half the lemongrass, half the garlic, fish sauce, sugar and salt for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil over medium high and fry the rest of the lemongrass, garlic and chili 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry 6 to 8 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Add the onion and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until the sauce clings.
Serve hot with rice.

citations.source: Helen's Recipes, Gà Xào Sả Ớt

recipes.curationNote: Single source (Helen's Recipes), 500 g chicken. Thigh chosen for juiciness, as most home cooks use.

recipes.name: Tôm Rim (Caramelized Shrimp)
recipes.flavorProfile: Small shrimp simmered in fish sauce and sugar until lacquered, sweet, salty and peppery, a little goes a long way over rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp bring protein, selenium and vitamin B12; the glaze is salty, so it is eaten a few at a time with plain rice and soup.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Marinate the shrimp with fish sauce, sugar and pepper for 15 to 20 minutes.
Fry the garlic and shallot in the oil over medium heat 1 to 2 minutes until golden.
Add the shrimp and marinade and cook 10 to 15 minutes over medium low, turning, until the liquid reduces to a sticky glaze.
Scatter the scallion over and serve with rice.
recipes.curationNote: Single source (Vicky Pham), 2 lb shrimp for 8 servings as a rice accompaniment.

recipes.name: Sườn Ram Mặn (Caramelized Pork Ribs)
recipes.flavorProfile: Short pieces of spare rib blanched, then braised in caramel, fish sauce and coconut water until the meat is tender and the glaze is dark and sticky.
recipes.healthBenefit: The ribs bring protein, zinc and B vitamins; they are fatty and the glaze is salty sweet, so serve with plenty of rice and vegetables.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tbsp in the marinade, 2 tbsp for the caramel
fresh coconut water (nước dừa); coconut soda is the common stand-in abroad

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for about 8 minutes, drain and rinse.
Toss the ribs with shallot, garlic, fish sauce, pepper and 1 tbsp sugar and leave 20 minutes.
Melt the remaining 2 tbsp sugar in a heavy pan over medium heat 3 to 5 minutes into an amber caramel, add the ribs and turn to coat.
Add the coconut water and water and braise uncovered 30 to 40 minutes, turning, until the sauce is a thick glaze.
Top with scallion and serve with rice.
recipes.curationNote: Single source (Vicky Pham, opened through WebFetch): 2 lb ribs, 8-minute blanch, 30 to 40 minute braise.

recipes.name: Chả Cá Lã Vọng (Turmeric Fish with Dill)
recipes.flavorProfile: Golden turmeric and galangal fish sizzled with heaps of dill and spring onion, eaten over rice noodles with herbs, peanuts and a pungent shrimp paste dip.
recipes.healthBenefit: White fish brings lean protein and the big handfuls of dill and spring onion add greens; the shrimp paste dip is salty, so use it sparingly.

ingredients.name: mẻ (fermented rice)
ingredients.prepNote: plain yogurt is the usual stand-in

ingredients.name: mắm tôm (fermented shrimp paste)

recipes.flavorProfile: Soft split mung beans in a lightly thickened sweet syrup with pandan, topped with coconut milk, eaten warm or over ice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mung beans bring plant protein, fibre and folate; it is sweetened, so it is a dessert portion.
instructions: Simmer the mung beans in the water with the pandan 25 to 30 minutes, until soft but holding shape.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Stir in the starch slurry and cook 2 to 3 minutes until it turns clear and lightly thick.
Warm the coconut milk with the salt.
Serve the chè warm or over ice with coconut milk and sesame on top.
recipes.curationNote: Single source (Helen's Recipes, chè hoa cau, the northern mung bean chè).

recipes.name: Bánh Flan (Caramel Custard)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smooth, silky custard of eggs, coconut milk and condensed milk under a bitter dark caramel, often with a splash of black coffee over the top.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs bring protein, choline and vitamin B12; with condensed milk and caramel it is a rich, sweet treat.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Cook the sugar and water over medium heat 5 to 8 minutes into a dark amber caramel and pour a thin layer into 8 ramekins.
Warm the coconut milk, milk and condensed milk until steaming, not boiling.
Whisk the eggs and yolks gently without making foam, then slowly whisk in the warm milk and vanilla, and strain.
Pour into the ramekins, cover each, and steam over gentle heat 20 to 25 minutes, or bake in a water bath at 325°F (160°C) for 35 to 40 minutes, until just set.
Chill at least 4 hours, run a knife round and turn out. Serve with crushed ice and a little black coffee if you like.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the condensed milk and caramel.

recipes.curationNote: Helen's coconut flan, with the condensed milk the southern version uses. Single source.

recipes.name: Bánh Chuối Nướng (Baked Banana Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: A dense, moist, pudding-like cake of ripe bananas, soaked bread and coconut milk, caramelized on top and fragrant with vanilla.
recipes.healthBenefit: Bananas bring potassium and the eggs and milk add protein; with sugar, butter and bread it is a sweet treat.

components.note: day-old rolls, torn and soaked

ingredients.cutPrep: very ripe, half mashed and half sliced

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Tear the bread and soak it in the coconut milk and milk 20 to 30 minutes, then mash smooth.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and butter a 23 cm cake tin.
Mix in the mashed bananas, eggs, most of the sugar, melted butter, vanilla and salt.
Pour into the tin, lay the banana slices on top and sprinkle with the rest of the sugar.
Bake 60 to 75 minutes until set and deep golden, then cool fully before slicing.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the sugar on and in the cake.

recipes.curationNote: Single source (Helen's Recipes), the bread pudding style. The bread points at the bánh mì base.

recipes.name: Cà Phê Sữa Đá (Iced Milk Coffee)
recipes.flavorProfile: Strong, dark coffee dripped slowly through a phin over sweet condensed milk, stirred and poured over ice, bitter, sweet and creamy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Coffee brings caffeine and a little potassium; the condensed milk makes it a sweet drink.

ingredients.prepNote: from 2 tbsp dark-roast ground coffee dripped through a phin

instructions: Put the condensed milk in a glass and set the phin filter on top with the ground coffee.
Pour in a splash of hot water, wait 30 seconds for the grounds to bloom, then fill the filter.
Let it drip 4 to 5 minutes.
Stir the coffee into the condensed milk and pour over a glass of ice.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Cà Phê Sữa Đá
Viet World Kitchen, Vietnamese Iced Coffee Tips

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham and Andrea Nguyen compared: about 2 tbsp coffee to 2 tbsp condensed milk, phin dripped. Ice written as water.

recipes.name: Cà Phê Trứng (Egg Coffee)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot strong coffee under a thick, sweet, custardy foam of egg yolk whipped with condensed milk, like a liquid tiramisu.
recipes.healthBenefit: The yolk brings choline and vitamin B12 and the coffee caffeine; with condensed milk it is a sweet treat.

ingredients.prepNote: use a very fresh or pasteurised egg

instructions: Drip the coffee into a small cup set in a bowl of hot water to keep it warm.
Whisk the yolk with the condensed milk, sugar and vanilla 3 to 5 minutes, by hand or with a mixer, until pale, thick and doubled.
Spoon the foam over the hot coffee.
Eat the foam with a spoon, then drink the coffee through it.
recipes.curationNote: Single source (Hungry Huy). Born at Café Giảng in Hà Nội in the 1940s, as his page tells it.

recipes.name: Sinh Tố Bơ (Avocado Shake)
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, cold, pale green shake of ripe avocado blended with ice, milk and condensed milk, creamy and sweet.
recipes.healthBenefit: Avocado brings monounsaturated fat, fibre and potassium; the condensed milk adds sugar, so it is a sweet drink.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Put the avocado, condensed milk, milk and ice in a blender.
Blend 30 to 60 seconds until thick and smooth.
Taste and add a little more condensed milk or milk if needed.
Pour into glasses and serve right away.

citations.source: Viet World Kitchen, Avocado Shake (Sinh Tố Bơ)

recipes.curationNote: Single source (Andrea Nguyen). Written as builderType smoothie since it is a blended fruit drink.

recipes.name: Bánh Da Lợn (Steamed Layer Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bouncy, chewy steamed layers of green pandan and golden mung bean, sweet with coconut milk, peeled apart one layer at a time.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly starch and sugar with a little protein from the mung beans; a sweet treat.

ingredients.cutPrep: split and peeled, soaked and steamed

ingredients.name: pandan leaves
ingredients.cutPrep: blended with 250 ml water and strained

instructions: Warm the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt until the sugar dissolves, and cool to warm.
Whisk this into the tapioca starch and rice flour for a thin batter, then divide it in two.
Blend the steamed mung beans into one half, and the pandan juice into the other.
Oil a 20 cm tin and steam a thin layer of green batter 5 to 7 minutes until set, then a layer of yellow, alternating to the top.
Steam the last layer 10 to 15 minutes, cool completely, at least 4 hours, and slice with an oiled knife.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tapioca starch and rice flour.
From the syrup in the batter.

recipes.curationNote: Single source (Helen's Recipes).

recipes.name: Sữa Đậu Nành (Soy Milk)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fresh, warm soy milk scented with pandan and lightly sweetened, creamy and nutty, sold in bags from street carts in the morning.
recipes.healthBenefit: Soy milk brings plant protein and some potassium and folate; homemade, it carries no added calcium unless you add it.

ingredients.cutPrep: soaked 8 to 12 hours and skins rubbed off

instructions: Drain the soaked beans and blend them with the water in batches 1 to 2 minutes until very smooth.
Strain through a fine cloth, squeezing well.
Bring the milk slowly to a boil with the pandan, stirring so it does not catch, and simmer 10 to 15 minutes, skimming the foam.
Take out the pandan, stir in the sugar and salt, and serve warm or chilled.

citations.source: Viet World Kitchen, Making Soy Milk and Tofu at Home

recipes.curationNote: Written mostly from description: Andrea Nguyen's page describes her method but does not give a full recipe, so the ratio and the pandan follow the usual Vietnamese street version. Needs a check against a full recipe.

recipes.name: Chè Trôi Nước (Sweet Rice Balls in Ginger Syrup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, chewy glutinous rice balls filled with savory sweet mung bean paste, floating in a warm ginger brown-sugar syrup with coconut cream and sesame.
recipes.healthBenefit: The mung beans bring a little protein and fibre and the ginger warmth; mostly starch and sugar, so it is a festival treat.

components.note: a little in the filling, the southern way

ingredients.prepNote: about 200 ml for the dough, the rest for the syrup

instructions: Steam the mung beans 20 to 25 minutes, mash with the sugar, salt, oil and fried shallots, and roll into small balls.
Knead the glutinous rice flour with warm water, a little at a time, into a soft dough like play clay.
Wrap each filling ball in a piece of dough and roll smooth.
Boil the balls in water 3 to 5 minutes until they float, then 1 minute more, and move them to cold water.
Simmer the brown sugar, ginger and 1 litre water 10 minutes, add the balls for 5 minutes, and serve with coconut cream and sesame.
recipes.curationNote: Single source (Helen's Recipes). Fried shallots in the filling point at the hành phi base.

recipes.name: Bánh Bò Nướng (Honeycomb Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: A chewy, springy green pandan cake with a crisp golden crust and a honeycomb of tall bubbles inside, rich with coconut.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly starch, sugar and coconut fat with protein from the eggs; a sweet treat.

ingredients.name: pandan leaves
ingredients.cutPrep: blended with a little coconut milk and strained

instructions: Warm the coconut milk with the pandan juice and sugar until dissolved, and cool.
Whisk the eggs gently, without whipping in air, and stir into the coconut mixture.
Whisk in the tapioca starch, baking powder and salt, strain, and rest 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) with the oiled bundt or cake pan inside for 10 minutes.
Pour the batter into the hot pan and bake 45 to 55 minutes until the top is deep golden, then cool upside down fully before slicing.
recipes.curationNote: Single source (Hungry Huy). Tapioca starch matched to cassava starch.
